text: Gaming cards aren't Desktop productivity cards, that's not new.. The average gamer person buying this card will use it for gaming, which will  run most games perfectly fine, hence the mad dash to get the card. Its not all about cranking the settings up to FULL either, most games will do better FPS with less settings! You also need a fast CPU and lots of FAST memory, not just a large amount of memory. Any desktop productivity person will not be looking at Gaming cards  to run CAD or Creative Cloud apps if they know what they are doing. This card will do fine for the average  gamer/video enthusiast that  needs to edit a 15 min of 4K drone footage or to post a youtube video. Remember video editing , as well as other software rending (3D, CAD etc.. ) requires a Fast CPU and fast memory not a gaming card. For the price this card makes sense for someone not spending 4-5 grand on a desktop PC that they barely get any benefit from. People buying  the $1500 cards are spending $500 on mb, $1000 in memory, 3 grand in monitors, $1500 for a CPU if you get my drift. Lastly, all these bench marks for any hardware, given the stats are very close, the small differences aren't going to be noticed all that great. In conclusion, non of this PC hardware is worth the money its sold for. Its a money grab for these companies. Supply and Demand working away!

text:
Honestly (and I never thought I'd say this) I'm kind of getting sick of new graphics card reviews. There's literally no point reviewing a product that the VAST majority of people who want one will never be able to buy, even if they can afford it at MSRP. nVidia already can't meet the demand for their current products, and now they're going to add more? Let them sort their sh*t out first, then when it's actually possible to find these in-stock for more than a nanosecond, I might actually have a reason to care. While it might be useful to the small handful of people who can get their hands on them, for the rest of us, you might as well be reviewing vaporware.

And don't assume we're all just going to buy them from scalpers or wait a few years and get them 2nd-hand from miners either. Personally, I think you'd be an idiot to do either, not to mention being part of the problem.

text: @fabiusmaximuscunctator7390  I've watched all of them and there is nothing shocking there. I don't agree with all of his arguments, but most of what he said makes sense. First, the 3080 Ti cards are cut down 3090s, not upgraded 3080s. Second, the market is what it is right now. Semiconductor pricing is way higher this year due to overwhelming demand from every industry, tariffs are very high for certain brands that get made in China, and scalping is ridiculous, so any card at the so-called "MSRP" is indeed a great deal right now. Nvidia only sells a small quantity of these founders edition cards to bring interest to the product. The actual manufacturers like Asus, MSI, EVGA and so on make the bulk of the product and they would barely get any profit at all at the same prices as the founders cards. All of the outlets that judge the "value" of a card entirely based on MSRP comparison are merely grandstanding to show how much they feel the plight of the average PC gamer. This only creates false expectations and as very few people can buy products at "MSRP" even in normal times. If you want to hate on Nvidia, do it for more important reasons like making limited use mining cards that will be e-waste shortly, their attempts to monopolize the market and strong arm manufacturers, etc. Complaining that a 3070 Ti that you can't really buy for 599 anyway isn't priced at 549 which you wouldn't be able to buy either is myopic.
author: @AlDim000

text:
​ @AlDim000  I don't want to hate on Nvidia, as it is getting old by this point. 
I'm disappointed about Linus. 
The argument of the defective die doesn't make sense. Every GA102 that doesn't fit the 3090 could have been a 3080 instead. Thousands of people are still waiting to get their preorders from September. 

Secondly the VRAM argument is also stupid. A 3080 needs even less VRAM to produce than the Ti. 
Thirdly the 3080 Ti is no Halo product like the 3090. It's just a barely faster 3080 with 20% more RAM that costs nearly double. So intelligent people buy a 3080, people who want the best or have money to burn buy the 3090. Linus even admitted with the example of the Q6600 that it made no sense to by the QX6700, because it was way more expensive, but offered no real performance gains. 

The 3080 Ti has never been a "good value" 3090 as it is lacking the VRAM to be that, but it is a poor value 3080.

Moreover he basically recommended scalping to his viewers. Luke didn't really know how to react to this. 

This is what shocked my about this video. I don't complain about pricing as Nvidia always plays an unfair game, but Linus should be on the side of his audience, but instead he's only defending Nvidia's practices. He even attacked GN and HUB. GN kinda made fun of his false accusations in their own 3070 Ti review.

Imo this has nothing to do with the current situation, but whom you are loyal to, your audience or the industry. I guess Linus has chosen the latter unfortunately.
author: @fabiusmaximuscunctator7390

text:
@fabiusmaximuscunctator7390  You're wrong on several accounts here.

According to fairly prevalent rumors the 3090 may be on the way to getting discontinued soon. The 3080 Ti has roughly equivalent gaming performance for $300 less and has a bit more room to allow for better yields, so it makes more sense as a product for gamers. Most people still wouldn't want it, but that's the point. It's the new flagship for gamers. And specifically selling slightly under-performing 3090 chips as 3080s makes pretty much zero business sense.


Also, $1200 is nowhere close to "nearly double" $700 and that's not how much a 3080 actually costs. Founder's editions are not available to buy for the vast majority of people and they were never supposed to be. "MSRP" pricing on the 3080 in particular was entirely a PR move and created false expectations, which have been happily nurtured by most of the press. If you want to see where the real prices are, look at EVGA's base 3080 (since that company's cards don't suffer from the same tariffs as other manufacturers). It is $850 with other 3080s topping out around $1100 before scalping.

Regarding GN, Steve actually agreed with Linus on a lot of points. Linus just puts the 3080 Ti more in the context of the overall market and 3090 while GN argues that Nvidia must make the Founders Edition card cheaper to discourage manufacturers from bloating it even more and tend to compare it to the 3080. Fact is, standard 3080 Ti cards from most manufacturers are happily sitting at the $1200, which shows that Nvidia actually set a much more realistic base price this time.

text:
Honestly LTT, I get your approach to Nvidia's MSRP. But I think it's flawed messy the way you've been explaining it on the WAN show, 3080tie and 3070tie video's.

First of all. Although Nvidia isn't the manufacturer, for all intents and purposes they are in this specific case, especially under EU law (can't judge on Canadian or US).

2. You cannot mix the second hand/scalper market with the prices Nvidia sets for their products. Even though a product is only a day old and not out of packaging. If resold it's second hand. Nvidia isn't in this market, although. They sell their FE's at MSRP and this that is the baseline price. What their board partners do is up to them.

With that out of the way, however you look at it Nvidia made a mistake with their MSRP and either the 3080 & 3070 (MSRP = too low) are the mistake or the Tie-variants (MSRP = too high) are the mistake.

Looking at previous pricing of normal vs Tie-variants the difference between te two are too big. This was the case in the 20-series as well, looking at the previous generations like the 9- and 10-series.

Maybe it's a strategious move by Nvidia. That would mean it's not a mistake. But Nvidia are just assholes, a suffix that should always be applied to word "corporate".

Anyhow. 

Because we are at the mercy of corporate assholes. Especially a channel like LTT, should call out these assholes for their bullshit. And both the 3070 tie and 3080 tie should not get a buying recommendation.

And LTT should never condone scalping, which you kind of did do in the WAN show. Even though I know you didn't mean it that way.

Current pricing is atrocious, and Nvidia playing the good guy last year knowing fully that a global chipshortage was there or at least comingshoupd have made them open in their communication.

Intel, AMD and especially Nvidia are corporate assholes, all of them. They will create hype for their product no matter what. But this time they went too far.

Especially Nvidia. AMD and Intel not so much. AMD released the 6600 series on mobile with is a fine move with people using laptops to game on more and more.

Intel might bring extra competition to the space before the end of the year. And Nvidia is up selling their 3080 and 3070 chips at a significant mark up.

text:
@ossharkuenmeursault5609  The market is in a diffferent place, true. Prices are not what they used to be, true. But I'm writing about the price increase to performance increase ratio. This is what sucks. This is what makes these card not at all a good value

Also, their designations. The 3080 Ti is not in any way meant to be an alternative to the 3090. They have different purposes. The 3090 is not for gaming, it's for production. 3080's are for gaming. So the comparrison must be made between them ( 3080's ) when talking about value. And only between them. You would not compare a pick-up truck to a city car or a sports car when judging it's value. Same for the 3070 Ti and 3070.

Also, when judging value you should ( please read must ) compare the MSRP prices. Anything else is just market instability / lack of supply money added, that contribute in absolutely no way to the technical and real value of the product. 

Is a MSRP 3070 Ti cheaper than any other scalped 3070 or 3080 ? Duuh, yeah. Does that make it a good value ? No. It only makes it affordable ( yeah, in the current market, for better or for worse, it's affordable ). And that is all

Is a MSRP 3080 Ti cheaper than any other scalped 3080 or 3090 ? Duuuh, yeah. Does that make it a good value ? No, it only makes it affordable ( yeah, in the current market, for better or for worse, it's affordable ). And that is all

Should anyone recommend these cards and deem them good value ? No. Should anyone say : Hey, it's totally a rip-off, but unforntunatelly you cannot find something better for the money ? Sadly, yes. But, again, that does not mean good value. It only means the less evil. For a while, of course, untill they all run out of stock

text:
What have we learned from these Ti iterations? Well fro the 3070 Ti you get...~10% on average uplift in game performance and negligible difference in productivity meaning for every 1% of performance it is worth $10 more in the 3070 to 3070 ti range of which a majority of that goes through the faster GDDR6X memory and minor GPU die difference. For the 3080 to 3080 Ti you get ~10% game performance boost and ~15~20% productivity uplift which comes down to ~$50-$65 per 1% uplift where most of that goes to the GPU die difference but not so much the 2gb more vram.

In a perfect world where GPU shortages aren't a thing, people aren't scrambling to get their hands on mostly paper release minuscule amounts of hardware, I highly doubt Linus would have had the same outlook on either of these GPU compared to other Ti iterations in history that typically show a more cushy 20% increase in performance with more reasonable price variances.

text:
To be fair, even other reviewers like Gamers Nexus thought similarish with earlier pre-Ti cards that weren't good deals on the market if it wasn't for the shortage, like the 6700 XT and RTX 3060, just not that you should simply buy it, just more of "that's how the market is," being more negative and not suggesting gamers just go mob after a GPU in the hopes for MSRP.

The difference is that Nvidia is now affecting pre-existing products with these GPUs and are lessening supply of pre-existing products in favor of bad deals that allow them to make much more profit, especially with the 3080 Ti. So as a result, most reviewers are much more critical now and Linus finally evolved to where Gamers Nexus was at with the 3060 and 6700 XT... minus the "buy it now" mentality which I can see because, well, GPUs are incredibly rare to find these days.

Basically the perspective one should have now is if you don't have a PC, buy a prebuilt, and if you want to upgrade, same thing, and hurry until even the GPUs they get are in low supply and they have to pay expensive prices for their 3060 Tis and so on. If you're too late or poor-ish but have decent for now parts (at least a GTX 970/RX 570ish performance level), well, sorry, wait until 2022 or 2023. :'(

That said Linus' reasoning has been a mess and made it sound like as if he's an Nvidia shill when likely it's because he was caught off guard by Nvidia's lack of price reveal for the review and possibly that after the backlash thought he had a bit of even during the WAN show episode.  And of course the fact Linus is a rich fuck that gets 400 dollar experimental cables whenever he wants to a year and a half or more before he can talk about it, so he loses context on what budget is.

text:
Actually the people who bought the 20 series cards off people who sold them at a very low price expecting to get their hands on a 30 series card at launch got the last laugh. In fact the people who did that ended up in a GREAT position later in the shortage to buy a 30 series card even at scalper prices and only end up paying MSRP.

My brother in law scored a 2080 Super Gaming X Trio for $200, I bought a 2070 Super for $100 the week before the 3080 launched. Facebook Marketplace was full of cards in the sub $300 price range because everyone thought their 20 series card was going to worthless with the launch of the 30 series. text:
Sorry, even $599 seems like a ripoff.  I realize we're all punch-drunk from inflation and shortages and all kinds of scarcity worship.  But seriously... Computer hardware doesn't need to increase in price every time a new variant comes out.  The way it used to work is new tech would simply replace the old tech in its price brackets.  Linus, I wish you would advocate for more consumer savvy not just on the selection and quality side (which you do really well), but also on the more critical side of value.

Mid range cards should be in the $250CAD to $350CAD range.  The highest end cards should be no more than $799CAD.

What we're seeing right now is just a rehash of the same crap that's going on in the mobile phone space where pricing keeps creeping upwards.  Yes the tech gets better, but that doesn't mean prices should scale to infinity every time a new generation comes out.  It's not like 10 years from now I'm going to be looking at a market that still has 3070s. Please, stop running cover for video card vendors inserting models around existing ones to inflate prices, and bring focus back to how tech used to work: a more slot-like approach...

It did not help that when that footage was shot, prior to what was shown here, someone in the crowd asked if there was enough for everyone and the manager who addressed the crowd told them "No." I do not fault him for being honest, but this same manager also told the crowd, who by the way was not allowed to have anyone form a line or camp out on the side of the building per the landlord, that if anyone was to run from where they were waiting to the side of the building, they were excluded from purchasing the card. 30 seconds after he said "no" about there being enough cards, when they were allowed to form the line, practically everyone ran which is what you saw here. People were so pressed against the wall to form the line between the wall and a taped line on the ground that people were saying they could not breathe. I went in yesterday to Micro Center from the day of this comment to purchase the PowerColor Red Devil 6700 XT. Yes, I know that card is overpriced at around $950, but I bought it for 2 reasons. 1) Micro Center had up to 8 of those cards in stock for 4 days by the time I bought one, so availability was there. 2) I would rather not have to deal with waiting in line with crowds of people like what I just saw to get a card, and I will take that cost over having to mess with that situation. The card is going to be used for the last new computer I am building for the year and considering what is happening right now, it is for the best.

text:
​ @BigBoss-kk4sr  Sorry, BIG TL;DR here: Normally yes, but A) not exactly and B) tonedeaf given the current climate.

A)
The 3080 is already what would've been called a 3080(tie).
The 2080(tie) isn't a binned 2080, it's in fact a cutdown Titan RTX (It's a TU102, not a TU104).
The 1080(tie) isn't a binned 1080, it's in fact a cutdown Titan Xp (It's a GP102, not a GP104).
The 980(tie) isn't a binned 980, it's in fact a cutdown Titan(It's a GM200, not a GM204).
The 780(tie)... was a binned 780. Kind of. It's a GK110B instead of a GK110, but I'll call that good.

In the 70-range, the only comparable thing ever is the 1070(tie). It IS the same as the 1070... and the 1080. And is MUCH closer in spec to a 1080 than a 1070. So that doesn't compare well here.

The 60-range and 50-range cards are where we historically see the (tie) designation (at least since the GTX <number> nomenclature started, and before then was the wild west), and those are usually released alongside and have fairly considerable performance differences with their "base model".

B)
The GA104 apparently has a total of 48SMs on die. The 3070 released with 46 of 48 enabled. 2 SMs out of 48 is not a big number, certainly not enough headroom to warrant a $100 price increase. So, they make up for that by going with GDDR6X. There's two things that can be happening here: Option 1) their margins are better on the 3070(tie) cards, even with the GDDR6X. Option 2) This will let them sell an entirely new SKU to board partners for enough of an upcharge that the increased costs don't matter (to Nvidia), and the 3070(tie) FE will be made in limited numbers.

When Nvidia and partners can't push enough GA104-based cards period, they release a new model at the tippie-top of the stack for 20% more money. This is why it strikes people as a cash grab.

text:
@Andytlp  Anyone with any significant number of gpus that matters already knows. Happened 2013, 2017 so everyone knew what we were in for this year.

Having said that... Buying gpu's at this moment doesn't make sense. Jan-Mar ya sure. Gamers just mining on the side? Ya, go for it. Large scale ethereum mining starting today though? Not a great idea.

I don't forsee anyone selling what they already have, but with prices down on eth and prices up on gpu's, and POS bound to hit in 12-18 months, it's more economical to just buy 32 eth and sit on it.

Same with hdd's. I went out and bought 1.5pb worth of hdd's, a bunch of nvme's, started plotting day 1 on chia. Sold all my pre-release chia at $1500usd each and broke even in 30 days. Everything now with chias price drop is just HODL until it recovers now. Anyone starting today would be insane to buy any significant amounts of drives as they'd be so far behind it could take 2 years before they make any money back. Safer (and less work) to just to buy and HODL while the price is low.

In the case of gpu's, it's my honest opinion that miners barely put a dent in the supply. Nvidia's gaming division puts the number around 10% of gpu's. The real threat to supply in the 30 series launch has been gamers themselves. There's an estimated 220% increase in demand from gamers since the 30 series launch compared to the 20 series launch but they only have the ability to bump production 10%. This is the same reason that miners aren't buying Xbox series x or Ps5's but you still can't walk into a store and buy one easily or can you find one at a retailer online anywhere near msrp.

It'll be 6 month more minimum before supply comes close to catching up to demand without a single miner buying 1 more gpu.
